top_story: Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power grid if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz set the conditions for a broader confrontation, and Iran has now formalized that escalation by shutting the waterway to foreign shipping and imposing a sovereign toll regime at a critical global trade chokepoint. Israel’s offensive has widened in parallel, with strikes reaching Beirut on June 1 and forcing residents to flee after warnings that the capital would see “no calm.” On June 2, Israeli attacks in Lebanon killed eight people even after Trump announced de-escalation, underscoring the gap between political messaging and battlefield behavior. The regional picture is hardening into a cycle in which coercive state moves are disrupting trade, displacing civilians, and eroding confidence that outside declarations can contain the violence.
